summary: Unquoted search words ignore letter case however they are typed: README finds readme.md, TODO finds todo.txt, NOTES finds a folder named Notes. A capital is a preference instead of a filter: a search with a capitalised word is made in lowercase and as typed, and each result keeps the higher of its two scores, so names that fit the capitals still come first (README.md before readme.md, TaxExemptionController.java for TEC). An app typed with its capital (Safari) stays ahead of a file or folder of that name. What a search opened is remembered whatever the letter case, and for searches with quoted words. fff files and fff dirs lowercase their words too.
changelog: A capital letter in a search word made the word match letter case exactly, so `README` never found `readme.md`, `TODO` never found `todo.txt`, and `NOTES` never found a folder named `Notes`. Unquoted words now ignore letter case however they are typed, as the manual says. A capital is a preference: names that fit the capitals still rank higher, so `README.md` comes ahead of `readme.md` and initials such as `TEC` still bring up `TaxExemptionController.java`. Typing an app's name with its capital, as in `Safari`, no longer lists a file or folder of that name ahead of the app. A search also remembers the file you opened from it whatever the letter case, and when it has quoted words, which it didn't. Quoted words still follow **Letter case in searches**. `fff find`, `fff files`, and `fff dirs` match the same way.
behaviour_changes: An unquoted word with a capital no longer matches case exactly. On the old code README found only README.md; TODO, IMG_0001, NOTES, BUDGET, ROADMAP and RESEARCH found nothing or only names in that exact case; ÜBER and МОСКВА found only that spelling. Each now finds the names in any case. The same holds for fff find, Smart Folders and the file chooser, which all go through Engine::search.

A search that has a word of two letters or more with a capital (or, with folders in the results, such a folder token) is made twice in each search location, in lowercase and as typed, and each result keeps the higher of its two scores. Names that fit the capitals keep the score they had before this change, so they stay in front: README lists the README.md files and then readme.txt; TEC, USC, SVC still list the names with those capitals first. Names that are only found in lowercase rank by their lowercase score, so a better lowercase match (a name that is exactly the word) can still come ahead of an as-typed partial one.

Capitalised searches cost about two searches instead of one. Measured in a debug build: 1.5 to 2.6 ms in the 154-file demo folder (1.3 ms before); 32 to 70 ms against 20 to 33 ms for the lowercase form in a 30,000-file tree.

More results for capitalised words, and a longer tail under This Computer: TEC in the demo folder now lists 30 items, the two real ones first; the old code matched 13. The tail is the pre-existing absolute-path strict check (brief strict-check-scope-relative), now seen for capitals as it already was for lowercase.

With typos allowed, a capitalised word that had no match in its exact case used to show typo-only junk (LIB showed Budget.csv, ACME showed README.md). It now shows the real matches in another case, and the junk is dropped as for any word that has real matches.
With folders in the results (Any Kind, Kind Folder), NOTES/, /NOTES/ and main Src/ ignore case too, because fff-search reads folder tokens as words there.

Apps: typing an app's name with a capital (Safari, Notes, Music, Terminal, Xcode) lists the app ahead of a file or folder with that name, as the lowercase form always did. In a test fixture the old code scored Safari.txt 268, a folder named Safari 255 and Safari.app 250 for Safari; the app now scores 280.
Quoted words with Letter case on Ignore Case find every spelling ("README" returned only README.md before). Quoted words on Smart or Match Case, and globs, behave as before.

Tokens with a colon are searched in lowercase: Main.rs:42 as before but in any case, and git:Modified, Git:m, Status:M now act as the git status filter instead of fuzzy text. A capitalised Status: or G: on its own is now the modified filter, as status: and g: already were.

Search memory: a search is remembered under its lowercase, unquoted, glob-folded text. README and readme share one entry. Searches with quoted words or folded globs now get the opened-file boost; on the old code they never did. An entry stored with capitals by an earlier version still counts when the words are typed that way, through the search made as typed, but it can no longer be replaced: a file opened now is remembered under the lowercase text, and both rank on top for the capitalised spelling.
fff files and fff dirs: the words of the query are lowercased, so they match any case. Only the lowercase search is made there, so the order is the lowercase order.

A one-letter capital query (A) is searched exactly as its lowercase form. Words with a capital fff-search cannot match from lowercase (İ, Ⱥ, ϴ, ℂ, the Kelvin and Ångström signs, ẞ) are left as typed and behave as before.
left_out: A lone folder token in a files-only search with no kind or scope (fff find Notes/ --files) still matches capitals exactly: fff-search demotes that single token to fuzzy text, and the fold leaves folder tokens alone in file mode because they are normally filters there.

fff files and fff dirs do not make the second, as-typed search. Capitalised initials there follow the lowercase order, and with --limit the name that fits the capitals can be cut. They also still have no quoted phrases or glob folding (outside the brief).
Short ! tokens that fff-search reads as text (!Ab) are left alone, as the plan says for exclusions.

The memory of what a search opened is filed under the search location as given and looked up under fff-search's canonical spelling of it. On Windows these differ for some folders (short 8.3 names, as in CI's temp folder), so the new history test is not compiled there. The mismatch was there before and is not fixed here.
CHANGELOG.md is not edited, as the guide requires; the entry is in the commit message.
clippy with --features term was not run: nothing under src/term changed and no signature it calls changed.
review_fixes: Ranking, the main one. The implementation followed the plan: lowercase the words and add 10 points to a name that has a word as typed. The brief called the cost to initials 'slightly different' ranking; measured, it was not slight. In a 30,000-file tree of CamelCase, snake_case and spaced names, with 500 results shown, the name a set of initials stands for went from rank 1 to 8 on the old code to beyond 100 or off the list: LHMT 1 to 262, QAR 1 to 104, PLG 1 to 135, TVFT 1 to 114, DCRT 1 to 140, RMM 1 to 105, and RVR, EBS, FRP, RGT, PTO, MAM (ranks 2 to 8 before) were no longer shown at all. In a 36-file fixture TEC and USC dropped from first to fourth and third. fff-search scores capitals only for a word that has one, so no bonus added afterwards can bring these back: the names are outside the candidates the lowercase search returns. The 10-point bonus (case_bonus, CASE_BONUS and its test) is gone. Engine::search now also makes the search as typed (words_as_typed) and keep_higher merges the two, each result keeping its higher score. The same queries now rank 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, and 4, 2, 8, 2, 6, 4, while README, ACCOUNT, LAYOUT and the like still find the other spellings. Tests: capitals_say_which_names_come_first, a_result_found_both_ways_keeps_its_higher_score, words_are_searched_as_typed_too.

Apps. Apps are scored by the engine, not by fff-search, so they never got what fff-search gives a name for a capital. On the old code that already put a file or folder named Safari ahead of Safari.app when Safari was typed with its capital, and searching as typed would have kept it so. An app now gets case_fit: 5 points for each letter of a word its name has in the typed case, about what fff-search gives (measured: 18 to 38 points for 4 to 8 letters). Safari, Notes, Music, Terminal, Xcode, Term and TE now rank the app as their lowercase forms do. Tests: a_capital_keeps_an_app_ahead_of_other_items_with_its_name, an_app_scores_for_the_capitals_it_fits.

The search made as typed keeps tokens with a colon in lowercase, so git:Modified is the same filter in both searches and the old fuzzy-text reading of it does not come back as junk. One-letter words stay lowercase, so a lone capital letter does not run the heaviest search twice.
docs/manual.md, Ranking and limits: the sentence about capitals now says that names that fit the capitals rank higher, with README and TEC as examples, in place of 'between equal matches'.
Commit message and Changelog paragraph rewritten for the above, including the app fix and the remembered-search fix, which the first Changelog paragraph left out.
The comment in track_open now says which of the two searches a search is remembered under.
notes:
Checked. tests/finder.rs a_capital_in_a_search_word_doesnt_narrow_it fails with the src and crates diff reverse-applied (found == []). The engine tests live in engine.rs and go away with that revert, so the trunk's behaviour was emulated at the three call sites (search, list, track_open): capitals_in_a_word_dont_narrow_the_search, capitals_say_which_names_come_first, a_capital_keeps_an_app_ahead_of_other_items_with_its_name and a_search_remembers_what_it_opened_whatever_the_capitals all fail; the four pure tests are for functions that exist only with the change. Mutations: switching the as-typed search off fails capitals_say_which_names_come_first (user_service.rb first) and the 'as typed comes first' assertion; switching case_fit off fails the app test (Safari.txt first). check.sh printed CHECK OK before the rebase (432 passed) and on the trunk commit after it (444 passed in 16 test binaries, 3 of 3 known root-only failures). The rebase onto 17a460e had no conflicts.

Also compared old and final results for 2,034 generated capitalised searches (113 to 349 queries over three fixtures, each as Any Kind, files only and folders): nothing the old code listed that really has the words was missing, and no score was lower than before, except by a uniform 4 points in queries whose only capital is a lone letter beside other text (A !x), which changes no order. In the 30,000-file tree the same comparison showed differences only at the tail, and running the old code twice on one query gave the same kind of difference (187 and 171 results, 33 and 17 not shared): fff-search's cut of the candidates among equal scores changes from run to run. That was there before and matters to the brief search-truncation-honesty.

Doubts that remain.
1. This is a different mechanism from the plan of record, chosen by the reviewer on measurements. The cost is a second fff-search search for capitalised queries and about 45 more lines than the plan's bonus. If the owner prefers the plain version (capitals ignored, 10-point tie-break), it is commit 7ac4375, which lane-b's reflog keeps for now; the initials regression above comes with it.
2. CASE_FIT = 5 is fitted to fff-search 0.11.0's scores. If its capital bonuses change, apps drift against same-named files under capitals; the Safari test will say so.
3. Only Linux was run. Nothing platform-specific was added. The history test opens the real LMDB databases, the first test to do so, and is not compiled on Windows; on macOS fff-search keeps the base path as given (file_picker.rs, FilePicker::new), so it should pass.
4. For the brief folder-filter-any-kind: once folder tokens are real filters in Any Kind and Folder searches, fold_word_case must leave them as typed there (its folders argument is true for those searches today), or a filter such as /Über/ is lowered and stops matching, since fff-search compares filters case-blind only from A to Z. words_as_typed needs no change.
5. total_matched is the lowercase search's count; for a quoted search it is the number of distinct results, since keep_higher merges per location.
6. A legacy remembered search with capitals cannot be replaced any more (see behaviour changes). Passing no tracker to the as-typed search would orphan those entries instead, which is what the brief accepted; it would need a parameter on search_root.
